I'm looking at the 2x2 square with three red cells and one non-red cell, and testing a rule where each red cell's normalized position maps to a diagonal direction, then rays get shot from each square cell in that direction to recolor with 8.

Now I'm tracing rays in three directions from all four corners of the square, working out which cells each hits across the 9x9 grid before marking them all with 8.

content.text:
I'm working out the square's normalized position and finding the direction vector (-1,-1) based on the red marker, then tracing that diagonal from each of the four square cells (4,1),(4,2),(5,1),(5,2) to determine which cells to recolor 6, starting with the shot from (4,1) reaching (3,0).

Continuing the shots: (4,2) reaches (3,1),(2,0); (5,1) reaches (4,0); (5,2) reaches (4,1),(3,0). Combining all these into a union gives cells (2,0),(3,0),(3,1),(4,0),(4,1),(4,2),(5,1),(5,2) colored 6, with everything else in the grid staying 0, matching the pattern seen in the earlier example with three diagonal directions but here reduced to just one.
